newsitem.title: USA: Corning sees Q1 earnings above year-ago Q1.
newsitem.headline: Corning sees Q1 earnings above year-ago Q1.

text.p: Corning Inc said it now expects first quarter earnings to increase about 40 percent over 1996 first quarter results from continuing operations of $0.27 per share.
It said it also expects full year 1997 results will be up in the range of 25 percent over 1996 results of $1.50 per share.

Company chairman Roger Ackerman said, "the worldwide demand for our optical fiber is experiencing extraordinary growth and continues to strain capacity. Fortunately, the expansion of our Wilmington, N.C., manufacturing facility is coming on line more rapidly and effectively than we anticipated."
"We also continue to see strength in our other core businesses including environmental products and advanced materials," Ackerman said.

Corning also said that, in recognition of its increasing emphasis in the development and manufacturer of optical components, it has established a new Photonic Technologies Division in its communications segment.
Formerly known as the Components Products Business of the Opto-Electronics Group, the division designs, develops, and manufactures optical devices used in communications systems.

In connection with the formation of the new division, the company said that its board of directors today granted final approval for a new $40 million photonic-components manufacturing facility in the Corning, N.Y., area. Construction of the new 200,000 square-foot facility will begin in April and initial deliveries of components produced at the plant are expected by the end of 1997.
"Photonic components are an increasingly important part of Corning's portfolio of businesses," said Ackerman.
"We are committing significant financial and technical resources in order to take full advantage of the tremendous worldwide market opportunity for these devices."
